RULES:

* Exceeding it exits 3 and is NEVER absorbable by editing this file upward.
* 0 findings against a non-zero maxFindings ALSO exits 3 — debt that has been paid must
LEAVE the ledger in the commit that pays it, or the next regression hides inside it.
* This number grades FINDINGS. It cannot absorb a MISCONFIGURED run: the floors and the
two controls decide that first, and exit 2 outranks everything here.

CLOSED 1 — the element record is no longer a nested Y.Map SET AS A VALUE under a key.
Properties now live one-key-each in a flat composite-key map
(ELEMENT_PROPS_NAMESPACE, `${elementId}<NUL>${property}`), which both peers derive
identically without coordinating. There is no container to win or lose, so a
first-touch is an ordinary per-key write and disjoint properties MERGE.
The gate now prints `rival lost [nothing] · control held both edits=true`.
CLOSED 2 and 3 INCIDENTALLY, and stated as incidental rather than claimed as aimed-at:
both were DOWNSTREAM of the same rival mint. `read-leg-did-not-reach-store` was the
merged value never reaching a store because the container carrying it had been
discarded; `undo-reverted-peer-work` was client A's undo re-minting a rival record
that took client B's colour with it. One root cause, three faces.
STILL OPEN 4 — undo/undo-did-not-revert-own. An UNDO-STACK defect (C03 4.5-4.8),
not a CRDT one, and owned outside packages/sync-client. Left pinned, not hunted.
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-12 after §UNDO-REMOTE-ORIGIN + §UNDO-SCOPED-TO-AUTHORED-FIELDS:
0 findings, 1 -> 0. THE LEDGER IS NOW EMPTY AND LEAVES THE TREE ON THE NEXT SHRINK.
CLOSED 4 — undo/undo-did-not-revert-own. It was TWO stacked defects, and the first
was HIDING the second. Diagnosed from an instrumented dump of client A's history,
not from reading:
(a) REMOTE COMMANDS ON THE LOCAL UNDO STACK. C03 4.6 U-1 already REQUIRED the
exclusion and CommandManagerImpl already implemented it — the CRDT read leg
simply never REACHED it. initRemoteElementSync dispatches a PEER's change as
element.updateParameters; the initBusHandlers bridge calls _cmExec(cmd) with
no metadata, so CommandMetadata defaulted to {source:'HUMAN_DIRECT'} and B's
edits were pushed onto A's history. The socket.io leg never had the bug —
RemoteCommandDispatcher.ts:378 stamps {source:'REMOTE'} explicitly.
MEASURED: after ONE local edit A's history held THREE entries, all
HUMAN_DIRECT, so A's first Ctrl+Z was a NO-OP on a phantom entry, its second
reverted B's colour, and only its THIRD reverted A's own height.
Fix: an ambient remote-origin scope set by CommandBus.executeCommand around
the handler call and read by CommandManagerImpl.execute — the same mechanism
and the same synchronous-call-stack contract as the existing gestureScope,
and the same cross-package channel as __pryzmBuildingGenActive (L2 does not
depend on L1 and must not start to for one boolean). The REMOTE exclusion is
NOT weakened: A's own edit was never excluded — the probe found it present
and correct at history[0] the whole time. It was BURIED, not dropped.
(b) WHOLE-RECORD UNDO. UpdateWallDimensionsCommand.undo restored the ENTIRE
pre-execute wall snapshot (~12 fields via WallStore.restoreSnapshot),
including a materialColor the command never authored. Fixing (a) alone
turned undo-did-not-revert-own straight into undo-reverted-peer-work.
Fix: restore ONLY height + thickness (+ _renderVersion, for the
VIEW-DIRTY-CHECK string-equality rebuild) via WallStore.update(id, updates,
preserveMetadata=true) — same no-audit-drift guarantee, correct scope.
IMPORTANT — undo-reverted-peer-work was NEVER ACTUALLY FIXED by the RIVAL-MINT
commit; it was MASKED. The gate presses Ctrl+Z ONCE, and pre-fix that one press
landed on a phantom no-op entry. The pre-fix probe shows the SECOND press reverting
B's colour #c0ffee -> #aabbcc all along. Recorded because the earlier entry above
claims it closed incidentally, and that claim was true of the READING, not the CODE.
Defect (b) is NOT collaboration-specific. The same clobber fires single-user whenever
a later edit touches a field an earlier command snapshotted and the user undoes back
past it. Concurrency only made it deterministic enough to see.
Regression proof: packages/command-registry/__tests__/remoteOriginUndoExclusion.test.ts
(9 cases). TWO POSITIVE CONTROLS reproduce the pre-fix paths verbatim and assert they
STILL fail — the unmarked-remote dispatch still buries A's gesture, and the
restoreSnapshot undo still clobbers the peer's colour — so a green run cannot mean
'this scenario never had a defect'. Plus a single-user arm, a flag-does-not-leak arm,
a throw-inside-the-scope arm, and an arm proving explicit {source:'REMOTE'} is intact.
NOT PROVEN by this change, stated rather than left as an absence:
* THE RING BUFFER's copy of the same clobber. The wall.updateDimensions bridge pushes
a whole-record PatchPair (value: structuredClone(after) / before,
initBusHandlers.ts ~1090-1100), so a RING-FIRST Ctrl+Z can still revert a field the
command did not author. This harness certifies the LEGACY stack (world.ts's ring
buffer is a recording stand-in), so the ring path is UNMEASURED here and the fix
above does not touch it. apps/editor is outside this lane's territory.
* The OTHER whole-record undos. Only UpdateWallDimensionsCommand was fixed, because
only it is on the measured path. `grep -l restoreSnapshot packages/command-registry`
will find siblings with the same shape; none is proven either way by this run.
Regression proof: packages/sync-client/__tests__/rival-record-mint.test.ts, which
carries a POSITIVE CONTROL reproducing the pre-fix nested get-or-create verbatim and
asserting it STILL loses the property — so a green run cannot mean 'this scenario
never lost anything'.
SCOPE CAVEAT, stated rather than padded away. THE WIRE IS SIMULATED — updates cross by
Y.applyUpdate(encodeStateAsUpdate), not a WebSocket. Latency, reordering, loss and server
linearisation are NOT MEASURED and the gate prints them as not-measured on every run. The
real-socket question is owned by tools/ga-gate/check-collab-graph-integrity.ts, which is
GREEN; it measures the DOCUMENT and this gate measures the STORE and the UNDO STACKS.
Neither subsumes the other. C66 §1: no capacity tier moves CLAIMED -> HELD on this evidence,
and C8 remains FAIL — BLOCKED on the founder decision in L-391-COLLAB-DEPLOY-DECISION.md.
